summary: Implemented merge() in settings/merge.py per ADR-004: recursive dict merge, lists and scalars replaced, None override removes the key, inputs never mutated (results are deep-copied so they share no mutable objects with the layers). Added tests covering each rule plus load() layering; all 7 tests pass.
assumptions: An override of None for a key absent from base is a no-op (nothing to remove).
When an override dict replaces a non-dict (or missing) base value, it is merged into an empty dict so nested None markers are dropped rather than stored as None.
A non-dict override value replaces a dict base value entirely (ADR-004: any other value replaces).
'Never mutates either input' is extended to no aliasing: the result is deep-copied so later mutation of the result cannot alter cached layers.
None values present in the base layer itself are kept as-is; only None in the override signals removal.
